items.name: Black Bean Tomato Corn Pot
steps: Rinse the cooked black beans and prepare the tomatoes, chopped and corn kernels.
Warm the olive oil, bloom the cumin, and cook the vegetables until they begin to soften.
Add the beans and fresh cilantro; turn everything through the seasoned oil.
Pour in the water, add rock salt, and simmer until the flavors combine and the beans are very tender.
Mash a small portion to thicken the sauce naturally, then serve warm.
items.guidance: Black Bean Tomato Corn Pot is a thoroughly cooked bean main with a moist sauce. Vata: serve warm, cook until tender, and add a little ghee if the dish feels dry. Pitta: moderate chilies and sharp sourness, favoring coriander or fennel. Kapha: keep the portion light, reduce added fat, and favor ginger or black pepper.

items.name: Simple Corn Arepa Flatbread
steps: Combine the fine cornmeal, rock salt, and additional rock salt.
Add the water and half the olive oil and knead until the dough is smooth; cover and rest for 20 minutes.

Brush with the remaining olive oil and bake or griddle until cooked through and lightly browned.
Wrap briefly in a clean cloth and serve warm.

items.name: Quinoa Black Bean Pilaf
steps: Rinse the quinoa until the draining water is mostly clear; soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Warm the Olive oil in a heavy pot and bloom the cumin.
Add the cooked black beans, corn kernels, fresh cilantro and drained grain; stir for one minute.
Pour in the water and add the rock salt; cover and cook on low heat until the grain is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Rest off the heat for eight minutes, then lift the grains gently and serve warm.

items.name: Black Bean Tomato Cheese Bake

Rest for five minutes and serve warm.
items.guidance: This bean bake is flagged because aged cheese is combined with tomato. Vata: serve warm with soft rice. Pitta: reduce tomato and pepper. Kapha: use less cheese. Compliant variant: omit the cheese and top with ground pumpkin seeds.
